bullets.title: Soft NFP + hawkish Fed = mixed signals; JPM raises 2H26 growth forecasts
bullets.body: June US job gains declined to 57k, but falling unemployment signals labor supply constraint rather than weakness — JPMorgan projects unemployment to reach 4% by early 2027, implying ~60bp higher policy rates under the Taylor rule. Despite the soft print, JPM raised 2H26 growth forecasts and expects Fed to trend rates higher as labor supply tightens; near-term stance remains patient. 2Q26 wage income growth ran at 4.2% annualized.

bullets.title: Debasement trade roaring back: Gold targets cut but structurally bullish; USD weakening
bullets.body: Post-soft NFP and Fed reshape reports, the debasement trade (Gold+, Dollar−, steeper curve) is reasserting. JPM revised gold targets down to $4,500/oz for 4Q26 (from $6,000) and $5,000/oz for 4Q27 (from $6,300), but remains structurally bullish into 2027. JPM broad dollar index rose 2.0% in June; EM FX fell 2.3%.

bullets.title: Wolfe: June core CPI likely prints 0.23% vs 0.3% consensus; Fed hold through summer
bullets.body: Wolfe Research forecasts June core CPI at 0.23% MoM (below 0.3% consensus) and headline at -0.06% on lower energy from the Iran ceasefire. Core PCE expected at 0.27% MoM with YoY run rate at 3.4%. World Cup adds 3-4bp via lodging; rent/OER moderating — softer labor data supports Fed staying on hold over summer.

bullets.title: Fed's Warsh turning hawkish: nine FOMC members anticipate rate hikes this year
bullets.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's June FOMC stance tilted consensus toward at least one rate hike by year-end; nine members now anticipate hikes. JPMorgan is debating Warsh's reaction function following Sintra remarks. ECB also likely to hike in September despite a downside HICP surprise.

bullets.title: Iran-US ceasefire removes energy tail risk; oil down >20% from peak
bullets.body: The Iran-US MoU (signed June 17) extends a 60-day ceasefire and reopens the Strait of Hormuz, eliminating acute energy supply disruption risk. Both Brent and WTI crashed >20%; JPM re-marks 2H26 Brent to $75/bbl (from $85/$80 prior) and retains $75 for 2027. EU refining margins surged to >$20/bbl vs. 5Y avg $12 on tight inventories.

bullets.title: Hedge funds aggressively de-grossing tech: record Info Tech/semi selling in June
bullets.body: Goldman Prime Asia reports Asia equities saw the second-highest monthly net selling on record (Z-score -2.0) in June, with Info Tech/semis dominating outflows and reversing all record buying from May. Japan saw its largest-ever monthly net selling (Z-score -2.9). JPM Morning Intel flags Mag 7 and Software at -2 Z-score selling; US Momentum down 17% from June 22 peak with positioning still elevated but rolling over.

bullets.title: S&P 500 earnings forecasts rising at fastest pace since post-Covid; bubble concerns emerging
bullets.body: S&P 500 earnings forecasts are rising at their fastest rate since the post-Covid rebound, stoking bubble concerns per StreetAccount macro. Separately, MSCI EM posted its best quarter since Q2 2009 (+23.3% in Q2) but gave back 1.7% in June as Fed hawkishness and AI valuation concerns pressured risk assets.

bullets.title: Memory upcycle accelerating: UBS raises DRAM/NAND pricing sharply; industry undersupplied to 2Q28
bullets.body: UBS raises 2H26 DDR contract pricing to +32% QoQ in 3Q26 (from +17%) and +18% QoQ in 4Q26; NAND raised to +30% QoQ in 3Q26. DRAM seen undersupplied until at least 2Q28 as 2027 bit demand growth (+36.2% YoY) far exceeds supply (+19.3%). Memory industry revenues forecast at $992bn in 2026 and $1,763bn in 2027, with ~$1.2tn FCF in 2027E. The 17% pullback from June peak is seen as temporary.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure remains the dominant alpha source; momentum shifting to memory and power semis
bullets.body: Per JPMorgan EM wrap, AI infrastructure is the dominant alpha source in 2026 with momentum moving into upstream materials, memory, and power semiconductors. Taiwan MSCI forward P/E sits at 22.2x, 48% above post-2018 average. MS recommends a barbell in European equities: maintain overweight semis/capgoods while diversifying into 30 non-AI compounders given 68% of EU long-only funds already overweight semis.

bullets.title: Meta's AI agent progress slower than expected; Samsung foundry deal ($6.5B MTIA) in negotiation
bullets.body: Zuckerberg acknowledged Meta's AI agent development has underperformed expectations over the past four months, with reorganization and job cuts not yet delivering results; benefits expected in next 3-6 months. Separately, Samsung Foundry is in negotiations on a >KRW10T ($6.54B) contract to mass-produce Meta's third-gen MTIA custom AI chips.

bullets.title: EM fund flows at worst weekly non-ETF outflows since August 2015; Korea -$95.8bn YTD
bullets.body: EM equity funds posted -$6.0bn weekly outflows with non-ETF redemptions of -$5.2bn — the highest since August 2015. Korea outflows accelerated to -$11.7bn in the week, -$95.8bn YTD cumulative. Asia ex-Japan saw -$3.3bn. Taiwan outflows picked up to -$4.4bn. India remains a bright spot with +$217mn for the third consecutive week of inflows.

bullets.title: China AI stocks correcting tactically in July but JPM expects August re-leadership on earnings
bullets.body: A-share semis/hardware corrected 8-9% vs CSI300's -3% over two days as Politburo meeting speculation drove rotation into consumption, property, and financials. JPM expects China AI ecosystem to reassert leadership in August on strong 2Q results; IT sector has the highest FTM EPS growth (+4.1%). Tencent at -2SD on forward P/E and MSCI China at -0.5SD offer accumulation entry. End-2026 base case: MXCN 100, CSI-300 5,200.

bullets.title: China structural: soft macro, housing won't stabilize, but high-tech manufacturing surging
bullets.body: JPMorgan's China mid-year outlook sees full-year 2026 GDP near 4.7% with domestic demand softening in 2Q — housing will not stabilize this year due to unresolved inventories and weak buyer confidence. High-tech manufacturing rose 15.1% YoY in May and contributed ~40% of industrial growth Jan-May. CPI at 1.2% in May; deflation risks could re-emerge in 2H.

bullets.title: Euro area PMI confirms cyclical recovery; growth pace set to double to ~1% annualized
bullets.body: Final June composite PMI revised up to 50.0, +1.4pts from May, consistent with ~0.8% annualized growth ex-Ireland. Spain leads at PMI 53.3 (+3.1pts); Germany at 49.5; France lagging at 47.2. JPM expects growth to double to trend-like 1% annualized in current quarter as Middle East drags fade, with EU GDP forecasts raised for 2H26 on lower inflation and strong employment.

bullets.title: ERCOT Batch Zero advances; power/AI infrastructure trade: SEI at value, WULF awaiting Kentucky deal
bullets.body: ERCOT Batch Zero was approved by PUCT with confirmation expected mid-August; previously indicated ~35GW baseload and ~65GW study demand, supporting IPP contracting for VST, CEG, and GEV. SEI trading back to value levels in mid-to-high $60s with three hyperscaler customers; low $60s represents value of existing capacity. NRG secured 5.4GW H-class turbines from GEV with Kiewit EPC agreement.

bullets.title: Tesla Q2 deliveries beat consensus by 18%; highest growth rate since 3Q23
bullets.body: Tesla posted record Q2 deliveries led by Europe, beating consensus by 18% — the highest growth rate since 3Q23 — raising hopes of ending a two-year annual delivery decline. Energy storage also came in ahead of MS estimates, supported by improving unit economics for utility-scale ESS and data center customers.

bullets.title: Private credit under pressure: $16B in withdrawal attempts tied to AI-stressed software firms
bullets.body: Private credit funds are facing $16B in withdrawal attempts amid fears over AI-pressured software firm defaults. Separately, Meta and SoftBank credit moves are described as exposing fault lines in the rising AI debt pile — a potential credit market stress signal for tech-adjacent lending.

bullets.title: Alibaba bans Anthropic's Claude Code; China-US AI tool friction escalates
bullets.body: Alibaba instructed employees to stop using Claude Code and shift to its Qoder platform, citing security concerns over features that can identify users with China links. The ban follows Anthropic's accusation that Alibaba accessed its Claude model via fake accounts. Microsoft is simultaneously merging Copilot consumer and enterprise apps to compete with ChatGPT and Claude.

bullets.title: SK Hynix removing price caps from long-term memory contracts; multi-year agreements expanding
bullets.body: SK Hynix is adopting long-term supply agreements without standard price caps, allowing spot market increases to flow through during shortages. Both Hynix and Samsung are extending contract durations from 1 year to 3-5 years; Micron is setting price caps at 2Q26 levels with price floors. Anthropic is separately in talks with Samsung for potential 2nm chip production and advanced packaging.

bullets.title: Trump declares PJM power emergency; UK 2030 clean electricity target slipping to 2035
bullets.body: The Trump administration declared a power emergency for the PJM Interconnection region (67M people) ahead of a heat wave. The UK is unlikely to meet its 2030 clean electricity target of 95%, with the date expected to slip to 2035 due to grid capacity constraints. China's energy demand forecasting is increasingly uncertain amid AI, EV, and emerging sector expansion.
